definition: The date on which daylight and darkness are of nearly equal length; unlike the equinox, it usually falls a few days later.
etymology: A modern learned coinage joining Latin aequus, “equal,” to lux, “light”: literally, “equal light.” It names the small calendrical correction to the equinox’s promise of equal day and night.
usage: Around the September equinox, the equilux arrives when the day’s light and dark finally come close to matching.
